title: Verify analysis dimensions against explicit rubric metrics
when_to_use: When the evaluation rubric specifies required calculated metrics or a structured scoring framework.
experience:
- **Extract Metric Definitions:** Before coding, explicitly list all metrics mentioned in the rubric and note their precise formulas.
- **Create a Cross-Reference:** Map each required metric from the rubric to the corresponding analysis step in your plan and verify your planned calculations match.
- **Validate Before Reporting:** After computing metrics, verify the outputs against rubric examples or expected units (e.g., percentage vs ratio).
checklist: Compare planned code logic to rubric definitions
Run a sanity check on computed metric values before concluding
common_failure_prevented: Performing a superficially similar analysis but missing specific metrics required for scoring (e.g., using a ratio instead of an absolute relative error).

title: Formalize derived feature creation for segmentation tasks
when_to_use: When the task involves proposing new dimensions or features for a segmentation or clustering model.
experience:
- **Document Feature Definitions:** For each new derived feature (e.g., 'transaction consistency error'), write the exact SQL or Python formula and store it as a code comment and report text.
- **Create a Feature Inventory Table:** In your report, include a table listing each new feature, its formula, its business meaning, and its expected effect on the model.
- **Cross-Check Feature Use:** Ensure all proposed new features are explicitly used in the clustering and/or decision tree analysis steps.
checklist: Document the exact formula for each derived feature
Create a feature inventory table in the report
Verify the new features are fed into the model
common_failure_prevented: Implicitly defining or inconsistently using derived features, causing gaps in the analysis and missed rubric requirements.

title: Systematically compare model versions when evaluating feature impact
when_to_use: When the task asks to explore whether new features 'improve' or 'should be introduced' into an existing model.
experience:
- **Establish a Baseline:** First, train and evaluate a model using only the existing/legacy features.
- **Create an Enhanced Model:** Train a second, comparable model that incorporates the new proposed features.
- **Report Comparative Performance:** Present side-by-side metrics (e.g., accuracy, silhouette score) and a feature importance comparison for both models to demonstrate the added value.
checklist: Build and evaluate a baseline model with original features
Build and evaluate an enhanced model with new features
Create a direct comparison table of performance metrics
common_failure_prevented: Building only a single model with mixed features, which fails to isolate and demonstrate the improvement attributable to the new dimensions.
